tools.name: SendUserFile
tools.description:
Send files to the user. Use this for any file the user would want to see — a generated diagram, a report, a screenshot, a built artifact — and you want it surfaced, not just mentioned. Send deliverables as they are produced, not batched at the end of the task: a complete draft or a meaningfully updated version of the thing the user asked for is worth sending mid-task, so they can follow progress and redirect early. Do NOT send routine working files — scratch files, debug output, partial fragments, or every incremental save of something you're still actively editing; each call renders a file card in the conversation, and a stream of cards for one file is noise. Re-send a file only when it has meaningfully changed since the last send. Paths can be absolute or relative to the current working directory.

Add a `caption` when a one-liner of context helps ("the failing case is row 42", "before vs after"). Skip it if the file speaks for itself.

Set `status` on every call. Use `proactive` when you're initiating — the user is away and you want this to reach their phone (build artifact ready, report generated). Use `normal` when replying to something the user just said.

Set `display` to choose how the file is presented. Use `'render'` when the user should see the content inline in the side panel right now — a chart, a rendered HTML page, a diagram, an image. Use `'attach'` when the file is something they'll save and open elsewhere — source code, a spreadsheet, a document for another app — and an inline preview would just be noise. Leave it unset to let the client decide by file type.

Files must already exist on the local filesystem — the tool sends files, it doesn't fetch URLs or render content. When unsure of a path, verify with ls first; absolute paths avoid ambiguity about the working directory.

Example: SendUserFile({ files: ["report.md"], caption: "Here's the report.", status: "normal" })

tools.name: Skill
tools.description:
Invoke a skill.

A skill is a packaged set of instructions the user or project has set up for a particular kind of task (deploy steps, a review checklist, a repo-specific workflow). Available skills appear in a system-reminder listing with one-line descriptions. When the task at hand is one a listed skill covers, call this tool first — the skill's instructions load into the turn for you to follow in place of your default approach; some skills instead run in a subagent and return the finished result. A skill that runs in the background returns only the agent's name — its result arrives later as a task notification, so don't wait on it or invoke it again in the meantime. Users may also ask for one by name (`/<name>`, or "slash command"); that's a request to invoke it.

- `skill`: exact name from the listing, no leading slash. Plugin skills use `plugin:skill`. Directory-scoped skills are listed with a path prefix (`apps/web:deploy`); when both scoped and unscoped variants of a name exist, pick the one whose directory contains the files you're working on (most specific wins; unscoped otherwise).
- `args`: optional arguments to pass through.

Only names from the listing (or that the user typed explicitly) are valid. Built-in CLI commands (`/help`, `/clear`, …) aren't skills. If a `<command-name>` block is already present this turn, the skill is loaded — follow it directly rather than calling again.

tools.name: ToolSearch
tools.description:
Fetches full schema definitions for deferred tools so they can be called.

Deferred tools appear by name in <system-reminder> messages. Until fetched, only the name is known — there is no parameter schema, so the tool cannot be invoked. This tool takes a query, matches it against the deferred tool list, and returns the matched tools' complete JSONSchema definitions inside a <functions> block. Once a tool's schema appears in that result, it is callable exactly like any tool defined at the top of the prompt.

Result format: each matched tool appears as one <function>{"description": "...", "name": "...", "parameters": {...}}</function> line inside the <functions> block — the same encoding as the tool list at the top of this prompt.

- "select:Read,Edit,Grep" — fetch these exact tools by name
- "notebook jupyter" — keyword search, up to max_results best matches
- "+slack send" — require "slack" in the name, rank by remaining terms

tools.name: Workflow
tools.description:
Execute a workflow script that orchestrates multiple subagents deterministically. Workflows run in the background — this tool returns immediately with a task ID, and a <task-notification> arrives when the workflow completes. Use /workflows to watch live progress.

ONLY call this tool when the user has explicitly opted into multi-agent orchestration. Workflows can spawn dozens of agents and consume a large amount of tokens; the user must request that scale, not have it inferred. Explicit opt-in means one of:
- The user included the keyword "ultracode" in their prompt (you'll see a system-reminder confirming it).
- Ultracode is on for the session (a system-reminder confirms it) — see **Ultracode** in the workflow authoring reference.
- The user directly asked you to run a workflow or use multi-agent orchestration in their own words ("use a workflow", "run a workflow", "fan out agents", "orchestrate this with subagents"). The ask must be in the user's words — a task that would merely benefit from a workflow does not count.
- The user invoked a skill or slash command whose instructions tell you to call Workflow.
- The user asked you to run a specific named or saved workflow.

For any other task — even one that would clearly benefit from parallelism — do NOT call this tool. Use the Agent tool (if available) for individual subagents, or briefly describe what a multi-agent workflow could do and how much it would roughly cost, and ask the user whether to run it. Mention they can ask for one with "use a workflow" in a future message to skip the ask.

Every script must begin with `export const meta = {...}`: a PURE LITERAL (no variables, calls or interpolation) giving the workflow's `name`, a one-line `description` (shown in the permission dialog) and optionally `phases` — one `{ title, detail? }` per phase() call, titles matched exactly. Pass the script inline via `script` — do not Write it to a file first, and do not also set the tool's `name` input (that selects a saved workflow); it is plain JavaScript, not TypeScript.

The canonical multi-stage pattern — pipeline by default, each dimension verifies as soon as its review completes:
  export const meta = {
    name: 'review-changes',
    description: 'Review changed files across dimensions, verify each finding',
    phases: [{ title: 'Review' }, { title: 'Verify' }],
  }
  const DIMENSIONS = [{key: 'bugs', prompt: '...'}, {key: 'perf', prompt: '...'}]
  const results = await pipeline(
    DIMENSIONS,
    d => agent(d.prompt, {label: `review:${d.key}`, phase: 'Review', schema: FINDINGS_SCHEMA}),
    review => parallel(review.findings.map(f => () =>
      agent(`Adversarially verify: ${f.title}`, {label: `verify:${f.file}`, phase: 'Verify', schema: VERDICT_SCHEMA})
        .then(v => ({...f, verdict: v}))
    ))
  )
  const confirmed = results.flat().filter(Boolean).filter(f => f.verdict?.isReal)
  return { confirmed }
  // Dimension 'bugs' findings verify while dimension 'perf' is still reviewing. No wasted wall-clock.

Before writing a script, load the `workflow-authoring` skill — the workflow authoring reference: script API and gotchas, resume, the **Ultracode** section, quality patterns, worked examples.

This session has the default workflow size guideline: medium — keep workflows under 10 agents. This is a guideline, not a hard limit — follow it unless the user's prompt calls for a different scale. The user can raise or remove it with "Dynamic workflow size" in /config.

tools.name: mcp__ccd_session__dismiss_task
tools.description:
Withdraw a background-task chip you previously created with spawn_task.

Call this when a suggestion you flagged is now stale, superseded, or irrelevant — e.g. you (or the user) already fixed it in this session, or you spawned a better-scoped replacement. To replace a chip: call spawn_task with the new suggestion first, then dismiss the old task_id.

Only chips the user hasn't acted on can be withdrawn from the queue. If the user already started or dismissed the task, the result says so (a dismissed task's copy kept for later is withdrawn too) — do not retry.

tools.name: mcp__ccd_session__mark_chapter
tools.description:
Mark the start of a new chapter in this session.

Call this when the work shifts to a meaningfully different phase — e.g. after finishing exploration and starting implementation, after a fix lands and you move to verification, or when the user pivots to an unrelated request. The user sees a divider in the transcript and a floating table of contents for jumping between chapters.

Use sparingly: a chapter should cover a coherent stretch of work, not every tool call. A typical session has 3–8 chapters. Do not mark a chapter for the very first message — the session start is implicit.

The title is a short noun phrase ("Codebase exploration", "Auth bug fix", "Test verification"), not a sentence.

tools.description:
Flag an out-of-scope issue for a separate background task.

Call this when you notice something worth fixing that would bloat the current change — dead code, stale docs, missing coverage, a confirmed TODO, or a security issue spotted in passing. tools.name: mcp__Claude_Browser__browser_batch
tools.description: Execute a sequence of Browser pane tool calls in ONE round trip. Each item is {name, input} where input is exactly what you'd pass to that tool standalone. Actions execute SEQUENTIALLY (not in parallel) and stop on the first error. Use this tool extensively to quickly execute work whenever you can predict two or more steps ahead — e.g. navigate, click a field, type, press Return, screenshot. Each tool's own permission check runs per item — a step on a site the user hasn't allowed either asks the user inline (and continues if they allow) or is refused, which stops the batch; if a step is refused for a missing permission, call that tool on its own (that call can ask the user), then batch the rest. Screenshots and other images are returned interleaved with outputs; coordinates you write in THIS batch refer to the screenshot taken BEFORE this call. browser_batch cannot be nested, and preview_start is not batchable — but if the Browser pane isn't open yet, a batch whose FIRST action is navigate with a url opens it (other actions still need an open page).

tools.name: mcp__Claude_Browser__computer
tools.description: Mouse/keyboard automation in the Browser pane. Clicks accept either `coordinate` (pixels in the coordinate frame of the most recent `computer{action:"screenshot"}` — reported with every scaled screenshot; equal to the image's pixels for unscaled ones) or `ref` (a `ref_N` from read_page/find). Whenever you intend to click on an element like an icon, you should consult a screenshot to determine the coordinates of the element first; after the tab loads a different site, take a new screenshot before clicking by `coordinate`.

schema.name: mcp__Claude_Browser__computer
schema.description: Mouse/keyboard automation in the Browser pane. Clicks accept either `coordinate` (pixels in the coordinate frame of the most recent `computer{action:"screenshot"}` — reported with every scaled screenshot; equal to the image's pixels for unscaled ones) or `ref` (a `ref_N` from read_page/find). Whenever you intend to click on an element like an icon, you should consult a screenshot to determine the coordinates of the element first; after the tab loads a different site, take a new screenshot before clicking by `coordinate`.

tabId.description: Tab to act on within the preview context. Omit for the fronted tab; get ids from tabs_context.

action.description:
The action to perform:
* `left_click`: Click the left mouse button at the specified coordinates.
* `right_click`: Click the right mouse button at the specified coordinates to open context menus.
* `double_click`: Double-click the left mouse button at the specified coordinates.
* `triple_click`: Triple-click the left mouse button at the specified coordinates.
* `type`: Type a string of text.
* `screenshot`: Take a screenshot of the screen.
* `wait`: Wait for a specified number of seconds.
* `scroll`: Scroll up, down, left, or right at the specified coordinates.
* `key`: Press a specific keyboard key.
* `left_click_drag`: Drag from start_coordinate to coordinate.
* `zoom`: Take a screenshot of a specific region for closer inspection.
* `scroll_to`: Scroll an element into view using its element reference ID from read_page or find tools.
* `hover`: Move the mouse cursor to the specified coordinates or element without clicking. Useful for revealing tooltips, dropdown menus, or triggering hover states.

coordinate.description: (x, y): The x (pixels from the left edge) and y (pixels from the top edge) coordinates. Required for `left_click`, `right_click`, `double_click`, `triple_click`, and `scroll`. For `left_click_drag`, this is the end position.

text.description: The text to type (for `type` action) or the key(s) to press (for `key` action). For `key` action: Provide space-separated keys (e.g., "Backspace Backspace Delete"). Supports keyboard shortcuts using the platform's modifier key (use "cmd" on Mac, "ctrl" on Windows/Linux, e.g., "cmd+a" or "ctrl+a" for select all). Page zoom shortcuts (e.g. "cmd+=", "ctrl+-", "cmd+0") are not supported - use the `zoom` action to magnify a region of the page instead.

duration.description: The number of seconds to wait. Required for `wait`. Maximum 10 seconds.

scroll_direction.description: The direction to scroll. Required for `scroll`.

scroll_amount.description: The number of scroll wheel ticks. Optional for `scroll`, defaults to 3.

region.description: (x0, y0, x1, y1): The rectangular region to capture for `zoom`. Coordinates define a rectangle from top-left (x0, y0) to bottom-right (x1, y1) in pixels from the viewport origin. Required for `zoom` action. Useful for inspecting small UI elements like icons, buttons, or text.

scale.description: For `screenshot` and `zoom` only. Scale factor in [0.1, 1] for the returned image; 1 (default) uses the full image token budget, 0.5 returns an image at half the width and height (~quarter of the tokens). Coordinates are ALWAYS in the full-resolution coordinate frame (reported with every scaled screenshot), never in the scaled image's own pixels.

repeat.description: Number of times to repeat the key sequence. Only applicable for `key` action. Must be a positive integer between 1 and 100. Default is 1. Useful for navigation tasks like pressing arrow keys multiple times.

ref.description: Element reference ID from read_page or find tools (e.g., "ref_1", "ref_2"). Required for `scroll_to` action. Can be used as alternative to `coordinate` for click actions.

modifiers.description: Modifier keys for click actions. Supports: "ctrl", "shift", "alt", "cmd" (or "meta"), "win" (or "windows"). Can be combined with "+" (e.g., "ctrl+shift", "cmd+alt"). Optional.

action_summary.description: A few words saying what this action does on the page and to what, for example 'Sends the drafted reply to pat@example.com' or 'Opens the Filters menu'. Set it on every left_click, right_click, double_click, triple_click, left_click_drag, key and type action. State the effect only, and accurately: no reasons, nothing about what you were asked or allowed to do, no passwords or other secrets.

tools.name: mcp__Claude_Browser__resize_window
tools.description: Emulate a viewport size in the Browser pane tab. Presets: mobile (375x812), tablet (768x1024), or desktop, which clears the size emulation and returns the tab to the pane's own responsive size. Custom sizes need both width and height. An emulated size applies to that tab across reloads and navigation (scaled down to fit when it is larger than the pane): reset it with preset "desktop" as soon as you finish testing. The desktop app may also clear a size you set when your turn ends, so set it again in a later turn if you still need it. A size the user picked from the pane's own Viewport menu is theirs and stays until they or you change it; leave it unless they ask. colorScheme (light/dark) emulates prefers-color-scheme on that tab; it survives reloads and preset "desktop" does not touch it, but the pane re-syncs the tab to the app's light/dark theme when that theme changes or the pane reopens; local documents and static HTML previews always render light. The mobile preset (and any width < 768) also emulates a mobile device: Android Chrome user agent and 5 touch points, so pages detect a touch phone; your clicks still arrive as mouse clicks. Reload the page after switching so load-time device gates re-run.

tools.name: mcp__Claude_Code_iOS_Simulator__control
tools.description: Run, test, and visually verify iOS apps in the iOS Simulator on this Mac. Use this whenever the user wants to see or try their iOS app — "run my app", "test this on iPhone", "does this look right?", "try the new screen" — not only when they mention the simulator by name. Simulator only: this tool cannot drive or stream a physical iPhone or iPad. If the user wants the app on their real device ("on my iPhone", "on my device"), build and deploy for the device with your normal build tools instead, and say the live panel only shows simulators. 'attach' opens a live panel so the user can watch — when the user wants to see the app, call 'attach' FIRST, before building: it is cheap, opens instantly on a booted simulator, and errors harmlessly when nothing is booted (boot or build, then retry it). 'launch' installs and launches a built .app — build it first, with the user's own build tooling or this server's 'build' tool when this session has it; launch re-attaches on its own, but do not rely on that instead of the early attach. Screenshots and tap/swipe/text verification are headless and need no panel. Don't open the panel when the user only asked to build/compile or to run unit tests. Coordinates are in device points (origin top-left); the 'launch' result reports the device's point dimensions.

Simulator only: this tool cannot drive or stream a physical iPhone or iPad. If the user wants the app on their real device ("on my iPhone", "on my device"), build and deploy for the device with your normal build tools instead, and say the live panel only shows simulators. 'attach' opens a live panel so the user can watch — when the user wants to see the app, call 'attach' FIRST, before building: it is cheap, opens instantly on a booted simulator, and errors harmlessly when nothing is booted (boot or build, then retry it). 'launch' installs and launches a built .app — build it first, with the user's own build tooling or this server's 'build' tool when this session has it; launch re-attaches on its own, but do not rely on that instead of the early attach. Screenshots and tap/swipe/text verification are headless and need no panel. Don't open the panel when the user only asked to build/compile or to run unit tests. Coordinates are in device points (origin top-left); the 'launch' result reports the device's point dimensions.

action.description: What to do. 'attach' opens the live simulator panel for the user — call it BEFORE you build or launch, as soon as the user wants to see the app: on a booted simulator it opens immediately, and otherwise it returns a clear, harmless error (boot or build first, then retry it). Do not skip the early attach because 'launch' also attaches — the panel should be open before the build starts. The panel is the user's view, not a precondition — 'screenshot' and input actions work without it. Skip it only when the user has no interest in watching; 'launch' installs and launches an .app (it also re-attaches, but call 'attach' early rather than relying on that); 'screenshot' returns a PNG of the current screen; 'tap'/'swipe'/'text'/'button' inject input; 'touch_path' performs a single-finger drag along an arbitrary path (eased curves, long-press-then-drag); 'touch2_path' is the two-finger variant for pinch/rotate; 'open_url' opens a deep link; 'detach' closes the panel/stream. NOTE: a 'swipe' or 'touch_path' whose start point is on-screen and within 4pt of an edge performs the OS edge gesture instead of a plain drag — left=back, top=notification shade, bottom=home/app-switcher, right=Control Center (mapped to the current interface orientation). Start more than 4pt from the edge to drag or scroll content near the bezel.

app_path.description: For 'launch': path to the built .app bundle (e.g. DerivedData/.../Build/Products/Debug-iphonesimulator/MyApp.app).

device.description: Simulator name (e.g. 'iPhone 17 Pro') or UDID. Defaults to the simulator already attached, else the first booted one. The first use of a device asks the user for permission.

udid.description: Alias for 'device' (identical semantics: simulator name or UDID). Pass at most one of 'device' / 'udid'.

bundle_id.description: For 'launch': bundle identifier. If omitted, extracted from the .app's Info.plist.

points.description: For 'touch_path': touch path samples in device points. First point is touch-down; last is touch-up. dt_ms is the delay before that sample (0-1000, total clamped to 30s).

points2.description: For 'touch2_path': two-finger path samples in device points. Each sample carries both contacts (x1/y1, x2/y2); first is touch-down, last is touch-up. dt_ms is the delay before that sample (0-1000, total clamped to 30s).

duration.description: Seconds. For 'tap', >0.5 is a long-press. For 'swipe', the gesture duration (default 0.3).

url.description: For 'open_url': URL or scheme to open in the simulator.

# Handoff: finish the Agent chat composer redesign

The composer is the message box at the bottom of the Agent chat pane: the text
field, the + button for attachments, and the Send/Stop button. Kenneth wants it
to work like the input box in ChatGPT and Claude: a + menu that lists the file
types you can attach, a field that grows to several lines, and (later) pickers
for provider, model and thinking level. Most of the redesign is already coded
and uncommitted in a worktree. This document says what is done, what Kenneth
decided, and what is left.

## Where the work is

- Worktree: `/Users/kenneth/Projects/JusPrin-worktrees/composer-redesign`
- Branch: `claude/composer-redesign`, cut from `jusprin-newui` at `170d1ae080`.
  Nothing is committed yet. Commit only when Kenneth asks.
- The worktree has its own `build/arm64` and `node_modules`.
- Uncommitted files:
  - `src/slic3r/GUI/JusPrin/AgentUI/src/components/Composer.tsx` (the redesign)
  - `src/slic3r/GUI/JusPrin/AgentUI/src/components/Composer.test.tsx` (new)
  - `src/slic3r/GUI/JusPrin/AgentUI/src/components/ChatNavigation.tsx` (menu
    can show an icon per row, open upward, and show disabled rows)
  - `src/slic3r/GUI/JusPrin/AgentUI/src/styles.css`, `styles.test.ts`, `tokens.ts`
  - `src/slic3r/GUI/JusPrin/AgentUI/src/visual/authoring.visual-cases.tsx`
  - `resources/jusprin/ui/design-tokens.json` (new `component.composer`:
    padding 8, gap 4, inputPadding 4, maxLines 8)
  - `tests/brand/test_brand_tokens.cpp`, `agent-docs/jusprin/design-system.md`
- Status: AgentUI vitest passes, 471 tests. The native app has not been built
  and run with these changes.

## What is done

- One bordered box holds staged attachments, the text field and a toolbar.
- The text field grows with its content up to 8 lines, then scrolls.
- The + button opens a menu above itself with four rows: Photo or image,
  3D model (STL, 3MF, STEP), G-code, Document (PDF). Each row opens a file
  dialog for that type. All four types already work end to end in the app.
- Send turns into Stop while the agent is replying.
- Photo mode (the composer used when the agent asks for a photo of a print)
  keeps its "Photo" link button and shows no pickers.

## Kenneth's decisions (2026-10-19)

1. **Sizes come from the design system, not from today's code.** The Figma
   file "JusPrin v2" and its Claude mirror, the Design System artifact
   (https://claude.ai/artifact/3zgiix8rAw3rXextQnR5UL, `tokens.json`), are the
   source of truth. Where the code's tokens disagree (for example the icon
   button is 32 in Figma and 26 in code, menu rows are 36 full-width in Figma
   and 32 with a 4 px inset in code), the Figma value wins. Changing the shared
   tokens is a separate task with its own handoff,
   `handoff-design-token-sync.md` in this folder. Do not fork composer-only
   copies of those sizes here; either wait for the token sync or do it first.
2. **Focus ring follows the design system.** The Composer component's Focus
   variant in Figma draws a 2 px ring in the `border/focus` colour around the
   whole box. Use that, through the existing focus tokens.
3. **Use the operating system's native file picker, with type filters.**
   ChatGPT and Claude both open the native picker from their + menu. On macOS
   the web view's `<input type=file accept=…>` ignores the filter and shows a
   plain dialog, so the page should ask the native host to open the dialog
   (a bridge message carrying the chosen type), and the host opens a
   `wxFileDialog` with the matching wildcard on all three platforms. Keep
   the browser input only as the fallback when the page runs outside the app
   (visual review pages, tests).
4. **Provider, model and thinking-level pickers: talk to Kenneth before
   building them.** Kenneth agreed the composer should let you choose the
   provider (when more than one is set up), the model, and a thinking level
   that depends on what the chosen model supports, and that these choices apply
   to the current chat only. He would like each provider to supply its own
   model list (from the provider's API) rather than a list hard-coded in the
   app. Facts to bring to that conversation:
   - Only one provider is active at a time today (AppConfig key
     `jusprin_agent/provider`).
   - Each provider has one default model in `ProviderProfile.hpp`
     (`gpt-5.4-mini`, `openai/gpt-5.4-mini`, `claude-opus-5-5`), and there is
     one app-wide `model` setting.
   - The host picks the model once, when it builds the Agent; there is no
     per-chat model.
   - No reasoning or thinking parameter is sent to any provider.
   - The setup page tells people "Which model to use is decided for you".
   Present the options and their costs, get his decision, then build.

## What is left

1. Wait for, or do first, the token sync (decision 1), then make the composer
   use the synced tokens: icon button 32, Send button 28 high with padding
   4/16, menu rows and popover exactly as the Menu/Row and Menu/Popover
   components.
2. Focus ring (decision 2).
3. Native file picker through the host (decision 3). This touches native
   code under `src/slic3r/GUI/JusPrin/`; keep the bridge change additive and
   use the capabilities list rather than a protocol version bump.
4. Pickers, after the conversation with Kenneth (decision 4).
5. Build the app and check the composer in the real Agent pane, light and
   dark, on macOS. Capture pictures for Kenneth.

## The design to match

- Figma file key `jo9J1sK9ZZ0vxncWnSp0vH`.
  - Proposal frame `1834:2216` "composer-redesign · proposal" on the Agent UI
    page (`1423:396`): ten cells covering idle, typing, multi-line, the + menu,
    staged attachments, sending, Stop, pickers, Photo mode, dark.
  - Shared component set `1197:5155` "Composer" on the Design System page
    (`9:153`), rebuilt with the new variants.
- Plain-text specs (one resolved line per layer), copied from Figma:
  `~/.claude/projects/-Users-kenneth-Projects-JusPrin/figma-mirror/published/ds/project/screens/agent-ui-states-components/composer-redesign-proposal.spec.txt`
  and `.../composer-states-attachments-and-sending-matrix.spec.txt`.
- Known gap: the Figma proposal still contains a few typed-in values that are
  not design-system tokens (gaps of 4, 6 and 8, a 240 px menu width, a 3x56
  scroll thumb, the 8-line limit). They will be fixed in Figma; when the code
  needs one of them, use the nearest design-system token and say so, rather
  than copying the literal. The two Claude artifacts have not been re-synced
  with the rebuilt component yet.

## Rules that apply

- Read `agent-docs/jusprin/design-system.md` ("Writing UI code"): every size,
  colour, radius and font comes from `resources/jusprin/ui/design-tokens.json`
  through the CSS variables or `ShellTheme`. A value with no token gets a token
  and a guard test first.
- Guard tests must be shown to fail first (inject the violation, see it fail,
  restore from a copy, not with `git checkout`).
- Read `agent-docs/jusprin/fork-stewardship.md` before touching any file
  outside `src/slic3r/GUI/JusPrin/`.
- No live AI model calls without Kenneth approving the specific batch.
- Leave this file untracked. Do not commit it or add it to any ignore file.

# Handoff: bring the code's design tokens in line with the design system

JusPrin's UI sizes and colours live in one token file,
`resources/jusprin/ui/design-tokens.json`, which feeds the Agent pages (CSS
variables) and the native shell (`ShellTheme`). The design system itself lives
in the Figma file "JusPrin v2" and is mirrored, value for value, in a Claude
artifact. On 2026-10-19 Kenneth ruled that the design system is the source of
truth: where the token file disagrees with it, change the token file. This
document lists every known disagreement and what to do about each.

## Sources of truth

- Figma file "JusPrin v2", key `jo9J1sK9ZZ0vxncWnSp0vH`, Design System page
  `9:153`. Variables hold colours, spacing, radius, elevation and text styles;
  components hold control sizes.
- The Design System artifact, https://claude.ai/artifact/3zgiix8rAw3rXextQnR5UL.
  Its `tokens.json` was generated from Figma's variables and matched them
  exactly at the last sync (2026-10-13). A local copy is at
  `~/.claude/projects/-Users-kenneth-Projects-JusPrin/figma-mirror/published/ds/project/tokens.json`.
- Component sizes are not variables in Figma; they are the sizes of the
  components themselves. The table below was read from the local copy of the
  Design System page, `figma-mirror/figma/spec3/9-153.txt`. Note: the Composer
  component was rebuilt in Figma after that read and the new read is
  incomplete, so treat the Composer's numbers there as stale.

## Differences found

### Colours

Light-mode values match. Three dark-mode status colours differ:

| Token | Design system (dark) | Code (dark) |
|---|---|---|
| success | `#4CAF82` | `#58B894` (`primitive.successDark`) |
| danger | `#E07080` | `#F07A8E` |
| warning | `#E8B84A` | `#E9B960` |

These colours exist only in the code, with no design-system counterpart:
`action.secondary`, `secondaryHover`, `secondaryPressed`, `secondaryText`,
`secondaryBorder`, `action.danger`, `dangerText`, `dangerBorder`,
`overlayScrim`, `statusSuccessOnAction`, `textOnAction`. Ask Kenneth whether
each should be added to Figma (then the artifact) or replaced by an existing
design-system colour. Do not delete them on your own.

### Radius

| Design system | Value | Code | Value |
|---|---|---|---|
| radius-small | 4 | `dimension.radius.standard` | 4 |
| radius-medium | 8 | `compact`, `container` | 8, 8 |
| radius-large | 12 | `window` | 12 |
| radius-chip | 4 | (no token; `component.chip.radius` 4) | 4 |
| radius-full | 10 | `pill` | 9999 |

names (touches every consumer and guard test) or keep the code names and only
fix the values. Renaming is cleaner but a larger diff.

### Spacing, elevation, text styles

Same in both. Nothing to do.

|---|---|---|---|---|
| Button/Icon | 32x32, radius 4 | `component.button.icon` | 26x26 | change to 32 |
| Button/Primary | 34 high, padding 8/16, radius 8 | `button.primary` | padding 8/16, radius 8 | same; check the rendered height is 34 |
| Button/Secondary | 32 high, padding 6/12, radius 4 | `button.secondary` | padding 6/12 | same; check height 32 |
| Button/Link | 26 high, padding 0/4 | none found | | find what the code uses |
| Menu/Row | 36 high, full width, padding 8/12, gap 8, no radius | `menuRow` | 32 high, radius 4, side inset 4 | change, but see the warning below |
| Menu/Popover | 280 wide, padding 8 top/bottom, row gap 2, radius 8 | `popover` | padding 4, gap 0, radius 8 | change, but see the warning below |
| Chip/Printer+Spool | 28 high, radius 4 | `chip` | 26 high | change, but see the warning below |
| Chat/Reply Choice | 28 high, padding 0/12 | `replyChip` | 28, 12 | same |
| Field/Number, Select, Form Row | 26 high, radius 4 | `field`, `select`, `formRow` | 26 | same |
| Field/Search | 38 high, padding 8/10 | not checked | | compare |
| Segmented Control | 30 high, padding 2, radius 4 | not checked | | compare |
| Tooltip | 24 high, padding 4/8, radius 4 | not checked | | compare |
| Swatch | 24, radius 4 | `swatch` | 24, 4 | same |
| Status Dot | 8 | `statusDot` | 8 | same |
| Progress | 4 high | `progress` | 4 | same |
| Tool Panel | padding 12, gap 8, radius 8 | `toolPanel` | padding 12 | same |
| Sheet | padding 24, gap 16, radius 12 | not checked | | compare |

Finish the "not checked" rows before changing anything, so Kenneth sees the
whole list at once.

## Warning: Kenneth rejected the Figma header menu sizes once before

On 2026-09-07 Kenneth reverted the header printer/filament chip and its menu
from Figma's sizes back to the current ones (commit "Revert my header menu
restyling: it looked worse and I could not explain why", on `jusprin-newui`).
The values he kept then: chip 26 high, menu rows 32 high with radius 4 and a
4 px side inset, popover padding 4 with no gap between rows. Figma's values
(chip 28, rows 36 full width, padding 8, gap 2) are exactly what he rejected.

His 2026-10-19 ruling says the design system wins, but it was made about the
Agent chat composer, not with that revert in front of him. Before changing the
chip, Menu/Row or Menu/Popover tokens, show Kenneth both versions side by side
(a picture of the header menu at each size) and ask which one he wants. If he
keeps the code's values, the fix goes the other way: change Figma, then
re-sync the artifact.

## How to do it

1. Work in a new worktree off `jusprin-newui`. Do not use another session's
   worktree.
2. Read `agent-docs/jusprin/design-system.md` ("Writing UI code") and the
   guard tests: `tests/brand/test_brand_tokens.cpp` (native) and
   `src/slic3r/GUI/JusPrin/AgentUI/src/styles.test.ts` (Agent pages).
3. For each change: update the token, update the guard test so it expects the
   new value, and prove the guard fails first (set the old value back, see it
   fail, restore from a saved copy, never with `git checkout`).
4. Rebuild the Agent page bundles and the app, and check every screen that
   uses a changed token in light and dark: the header chip and its menu, the
   Agent chat (composer, reply chips, tool activity), Home, the printer
   dialog, and the settings forms. Capture pictures for Kenneth.
5. Read `agent-docs/jusprin/fork-stewardship.md` before touching any file
   outside `src/slic3r/GUI/JusPrin/`.
6. Commit only when Kenneth asks.

## Related work

The composer redesign (`handoff-composer-redesign.md`, worktree
`JusPrin-worktrees/composer-redesign`) needs the new Button/Icon, Menu/Row and
Menu/Popover sizes. It adds one new token group, `component.composer`
(padding 8, gap 4, inputPadding 4, maxLines 8), which is not yet in Figma.
Coordinate so the two changes do not edit the same lines of the token file at
the same time.

Leave this file untracked. Do not commit it or add it to any ignore file.

I wrote both handoff documents. They are untracked files in the main checkout, ready to give to a coding agent. Changing the Figma proposal so it uses only design-system tokens is still blocked, because this month's Figma read/write allowance has run out.

**[handoff-composer-redesign.md](/Users/kenneth/Projects/JusPrin/handoff-composer-redesign.md)** covers finishing the chat composer:
- **Where it stands:** the work is uncommitted in the `claude/composer-redesign` worktree, and its 471 Agent page tests pass. The app hasn't been built and run with these changes yet.
- **Your decisions, as written there:**
  - Sizes come from the design system.
  - The focus ring follows Figma's Composer Focus variant: a 2 px ring in the focus colour.
  - The + menu uses each operating system's own file picker, with type filters, opened by the app. On the Mac the web page's built-in file picker ignores type filters, so it stays only as a fallback.
  - The agent must talk to you before building the provider, model and thinking-level pickers. The doc gives it the facts for that conversation: only one provider is active today, each provider has one fixed default model, and no thinking setting is sent to any provider. It also records that you'd like each provider to supply its own model list.

**[handoff-design-token-sync.md](/Users/kenneth/Projects/JusPrin/handoff-design-token-sync.md)** lists every difference I found between the code's token file and the design system:
- **Dark status colours:** three differ, e.g. success is #4CAF82 in Figma and #58B894 in code.
- **Fully rounded corners:** `full` is 10 in Figma and `pill` is 9999 in code.
- **Control sizes:** the icon button is 32 vs 26, menu rows are 36 full-width vs 32 with a 4 px inset, popover padding is 8 with a 2 px gap vs 4 with none, and the header chip is 28 vs 26.
- **Colours only the code has:** about a dozen, such as the secondary and danger button colours. The doc says to ask you whether each goes into Figma or is replaced, rather than deleted.
- **A few unchecked components:** search field, segmented control, tooltip and sheet. The agent compares those first, so you see the whole list at once.

**Decision for you:** the token doc tells the agent to ask you before changing the header chip and menu sizes. On 2026-09-07 you reverted exactly those Figma sizes ("it looked worse"), and today's ruling was made about the composer. The agent will show you both versions side by side. If you keep the current sizes, Figma gets changed to match the code instead.

**Still blocked: the Figma proposal.** It and the rebuilt Composer component still contain typed-in values that aren't design-system tokens:
- gaps of 4, 6 and 8;
- a 240 px menu width;
- a 3×56 scroll thumb;
- the 8-line height limit.

Your Figma seat is View again, and its roughly 20 calls a month are used up. That stops both these fixes and the re-sync of the two Claude mirrors (the design system and the "JusPrin v2" canvas). Three ways forward:
- Upgrade the seat to Dev, and I'll do it right away.
- Wait for the monthly reset.
- Have me drive Figma's own in-file AI through Claude in Chrome, which doesn't use the allowance but is slower and less exact.

Until then, the composer doc tells the agent to use the nearest token for those values and say which ones it picked.

content.text:
No, Figma doesn't draw it this way. Figma does give menu rows square corners, but it has no design for a keyboard-focused row at all. The square purple outline in your "after" picture comes from the code: its standard focus ring got drawn around a row that now has square corners.

**Where the design lives.** The menu in your screenshot is the "State=Actions open" example in the frame "header-states · chat navigation matrix" (Figma node `1540:3341`), on the "Agent UI · States & Components" page. Its Rename and Delete rows are instances of the shared Menu/Row component (`321:3113` on the Design System page).

**What Figma specifies.** Menu/Row has five states: Default, Current, Hovered, Disabled and Danger. None of them has rounded corners. Each row is 36 px tall and spans the full 280 px width of the popover. The only highlight is the Hovered state, which is a grey fill (`surface/subtle`) edge to edge, so square corners look right there. There is no focused state. In the "Actions open" example Rename is a plain Default row with no outline.

**Where the outline comes from.** The "after" picture was made in the `design-token-sync` worktree, which another session is using to apply the token handoff. That work changed the menu-row tokens to Figma's values, radius 4 → 0 and side inset 4 → 0. The Agent page's stylesheet has one global keyboard-focus rule, a 2 px ring in the focus colour drawn 2 px outside the element (`styles.css:53`). Before the change, the ring wrapped a row with rounded corners, inset from the popover edges, so it looked fine. Now it wraps a square full-width row, so it comes out square and spills past the popover's edges.

One caveat: I checked this against my local copy of the Design System page, read on 2026-10-13, not live Figma, because this month's Figma read allowance is used up. Since then, the only Design System component I've seen change is the Composer, not Menu/Row.

**How to fix it.** I'd keep Figma's square, full-width rows and draw the focus ring inside the row. The chat list rows already do this with `outline-offset: -2px` (`styles.css:643`). The proper version would also add a "Focused" state to Menu/Row in Figma, so the design covers keyboard focus. If you'd rather keep rounded rows, the change goes the other way: Figma gets a radius and inset again, which is what you chose for the header menu back on 2026-09-07.

I haven't changed anything in the `design-token-sync` worktree, since another session is working there. Tell me which way you want it and I'll pass it on to that work, or make the Figma change once there's allowance again.

entries.name: SendMessage
entries.description:
# SendMessage

Send a message to another agent.

```json
{"to": "researcher", "summary": "assign task 1", "message": "start on task #1"}
```

| `to` | |
|---|---|
| `"researcher"` | Teammate by name |
| `"main"` | The main conversation (background subagents only) |
| `"worker"` | Any agent from `ListAgents` — subagent, another local Claude session |
| `"worker [3fa9c1]"` | Same, plus its `[ref]` — only when a listing or an error shows one |

Your plain text output is NOT visible to other agents — to communicate, you MUST call this tool. Messages from teammates are delivered automatically; you don't check an inbox. Refer to agents by name — names keep working after an agent completes (a send resumes it from its transcript). Use the raw `agentId` (format `a...-...`) from its spawn result only when the agent has no name, or when a newer agent took the name (latest wins). When relaying, don't quote the original — it's already rendered to the user.

## Cross-session

Use `ListAgents` to discover targets. Every row leads with the agent's `name [ref]` — the name IS the address; there is no separate address syntax.

```json
{"to": "worker", "message": "check if tests pass over there"}
{"to": "worker [3fa9c1]", "message": "you, specifically"}
```

Send the bare name — a name that exactly matches one live agent or session (on this machine, on another machine, or in the cloud) delivers directly. Append the ` [ref]` only when the bare name is not enough — `ListAgents` shows two rows with it, or an error asks you to disambiguate (you typed only a prefix, or a session list could not be checked). A ref you did not just read from a listing or an error will not resolve, and if the same name also names an in-process agent, the bare name always wins — use the in-process one.

A listed peer is alive and will receive your message; messages enqueue and drain at the receiver's next tool round (its `ListAgents` row says whether it is busy or idle right now). A successful send means the message reached that session, not that its Claude read it: a session running in a different permission mode than yours holds cross-session messages for its user's approval (and may let them expire), and a session can refuse them outright — for a session on this machine a `[Cross-session delivery notice]` tells you when that happens (the tool result says when this session has no inbox for one to reach); for a Remote Control, cloud or Claude Desktop session nothing reports back, so never treat silence as agreement. Your message arrives wrapped as `<cross-session-message from="...">`. **To reply to an incoming message, copy its `from` attribute as your `to`.** Cross-session messages travel between SESSIONS: if you are a subagent, your send goes out under your parent session's address, and any reply is delivered to the parent session's conversation, not to you. The receiver reads your message literally in every case (idle or busy, on this machine, over Remote Control or headless): an `@` followed by a file path, or `@server:resource`, attaches nothing there, unlike in your own user's input. So never rely on `@` to deliver content: send the text itself, or a file with its own tool.

To hear when a session ON THIS MACHINE finishes what it is doing, pass `notify_when_idle: true` (from the main conversation only) — one-shot and opt-in: exactly one `[Cross-session idle notice]` arrives when it next goes idle (or exits) — shown to you, or only to your user when this session holds peer messages for approval (the tool result says which); if it never signals within the subscription's lifetime (it may still be busy, may refuse inbound requests, or may have ended abruptly) the notice says the subscription expired instead. Omit `message` for a pure subscription that costs that session nothing; include one to deliver it now AND subscribe. Never poll `ListAgents` in a loop or send "are you done?" messages instead.

Permission boundaries are per-session: NEVER ask a peer to perform an action that was denied or blocked in your session, or that you expect your own permission settings would block — a peer doing it for you bypasses the user's permission decision (cross-session permission laundering). Route blocked work back to your user instead.

to.description: Recipient: a name from ListAgents (append its " [ref]" only when a listing or an error shows one), a teammate name, "main", or a background agent's agentId

summary.description: A 5-10 word label for your own transcript row (not transmitted — the recipient previews the first line of `message`). Truncated to 200 characters rather than rejected.

message.description: Plain text message content. The recipient's human sees only the FIRST LINE as a one-line preview until they expand it, so make the first line a clear, self-contained sentence saying what this is about — not a greeting, preamble, or bare @-mention.

notify_when_idle.description: Ask a session ON THIS MACHINE to send you ONE notice when it next goes idle (finishes its turn with nothing queued) or exits — opt-in, one-shot, no polling. With a message: deliver it now AND subscribe. Without a message (omit it): a pure subscription that costs the other session nothing.

input.summary: Ask token-sync owner for menu focus fix
input.message:
Kenneth approved a fix in your design-token-sync worktree: a keyboard-focused menu row should get the hover grey fill, not the purple outline.

Why: your token change set menuRow radius 4 → 0 and sideInset 4 → 0. When a menu opens (e.g. the chat header's Rename/Delete menu), focus lands on the first row and the global rule `:focus-visible { outline: 2px solid var(--border-focus); outline-offset: 2px; }` (AgentUI/src/styles.css:53) now draws a square outline that sticks out past the popover's rounded edges. Kenneth called it ugly. The design (Menu/Row card in the Design System artifact) has Default, Current, Hovered (fill surface-subtle, full width, no radius), Disabled, Danger — no focus state. I'm adding a "Focused" state, drawn the same as Hovered, to that card.

What he approved for code (I'm not editing your worktree's uncommitted files, so please do it there):
1. `.chat-menu button:focus-visible` gets `background: var(--surface-subtle)` and `outline: none`.
2. Check HomeUI menus and the native header menus (Shell/HeaderControls.cpp) for the same problem; give them the same treatment.
3. Keep the guard tests passing, and add a guard that menu rows don't use the outside focus ring. Prove it fails first (inject the violation, see it fail, restore from a saved copy, never `git checkout`).
4. Capture before/after pictures of the Rename/Delete menu with the first row focused, light and dark, and send them to Kenneth (SendUserFile), saying which is before and which is after.

Also from Kenneth today: Figma is retired. The two Claude artifacts (canvas https://claude.ai/artifact/VCEppdwfT7v32W4beUxL1v, Design System https://claude.ai/artifact/3zgiix8rAw3rXextQnR5UL) are the design source of truth. Don't cite Figma nodes or propose Figma edits. Memory: design-source-is-claude-artifacts.md.

If this worktree isn't yours, tell me and I'll find the owner.

"""Find whole elements in the canvas's one-line board HTML by attribute."""
import re
TAG = re.compile(r'<(/?)(div|span|svg|path|circle|rect|line|polyline|polygon|g|img)\b[^>]*?(/?)>')
VOID = {'path', 'circle', 'rect', 'line', 'polyline', 'polygon', 'img'}

def element_at(s, start):
    """Return (start, end) of the element whose opening tag begins at start."""
    depth = 0
    for m in TAG.finditer(s, start):
        close, name, selfclose = m.group(1), m.group(2), m.group(3)
        if name in VOID and not close:
            if depth == 0: return start, m.end()
            continue
        if selfclose: continue
        depth += -1 if close else 1
        if depth == 0: return start, m.end()
    raise ValueError('unbalanced')

def find_all(s, attr):
    out, i = [], 0
    while True:
        j = s.find(attr, i)
        if j < 0: return out
        k = s.rfind('<', 0, j)
        a, b = element_at(s, k)
        out.append((a, b)); i = b
EOF

# Composer

The message box at the bottom of the Agent pane, following common AI chat apps: staged files, a text area that grows with the message, and a toolbar to attach, choose the model and thinking level, and send.

- You supply `value`, `onChange`, `onSend`, `onAttach(type)` and optionally `state` (`idle`, `streaming` or `unavailable`), `mode` (`regular` or `photo`), `attachments` (the props of each staged `ChatAttachment`), `models` with `model` and `onModelChange`, `thinkingLevels` with `thinking` and `onThinkingChange`, `onStop` and `placeholder`.
- One box with `space-8` padding, `space-4` between its parts, `radius-medium` corners and a 1px `border-subtle` stroke, on `surface-canvas`. Staged files sit inside it above the text, `space-4` apart.
- The text area starts one line high in `body-small` and grows a line at a time up to `component-composer-maxLines` (8) lines, then the text scrolls inside it. Enter sends; Shift+Enter adds a line. The placeholder is `text-tertiary`.
- The toolbar: on the left a `ButtonIcon` with `plus`, then the model picker, then the thinking picker; on the right a compact `ButtonPrimary` labelled Send. A picker is `label` text and a `chevron-down`, `space-4` by `space-8` padding, `radius-small`; it fills with `surface-selected` while its menu is open.
- + opens a `MenuPopover` above it with four `MenuRow`s: Photo or image, 3D model (STL, 3MF, STEP), G-code, Document (PDF). Each opens the system file picker filtered to that type.
- The model menu lists the models of every connected provider, each group under a `MenuSectionTitle` with the provider's name; with one provider the heading is left out. The thinking menu lists only the levels the chosen model supports, and the thinking picker is left out for a model without levels. Switching models keeps the level if the new model has it, otherwise it falls back to that model's default. Both choices apply to the current chat only.
- Send is disabled until there is text or a file; a file alone can be sent. While the Agent is replying the placeholder reads "Agent is responding…", Send becomes a Stop `ButtonSecondary`, and + and the pickers are disabled.
- Unavailable is different from empty: the box turns `surface-subtle`, the placeholder reads "Chat is unavailable" in `action-disabled-text`, and everything but the text is disabled.
- Photo mode (the printer chat, where only a photo can be attached) shows a "Photo" `ButtonLink` instead of + and has no pickers.
- Keyboard focus in the text draws a 2px `border-focus` stroke around the whole box.
EOF
echo ok

"""Replaces the five Composer instances in the composer-states matrix board with the new Composer, keeping their text."""
import sys
from htmlfrag import find_all
from composer_html import composer
p = sys.argv[1]
s = open(p).read()
NEW = {
    'State=Idle, Mode=Regular': dict(state='Idle'),
    'State=Text ready, Mode=Regular': dict(state='Text ready', text='Make the bracket stronger'),
    'State=Attachment ready, Mode=Photo': dict(state='Attachment ready', mode='Photo', placeholder='add a note, or just send',
                                               attachments=[dict(preview='Photo', name='bracket-photo.png', meta='PNG · 1.2 MB')]),
    'State=Streaming, Mode=Regular': dict(state='Streaming'),
}
spans = find_all(s, 'data-c="Composer:')
for a, b in reversed(spans):
    head = s[a:a + 200]
    comp = head.split('data-c="Composer:')[1].split('"')[0]
    key = ', '.join(comp.split(', ')[:2])
    s = s[:a] + composer(component=comp, **NEW[key]) + s[b:]
open(p, 'w').write(s)
print(len(spans), 'replaced')
EOF

"""Sets a canvas board's height in its file and in canvas.json, and reports boards that would now overlap it.
Usage: resize_board.py <canvas project dir> <board.dc.html> <new height>"""
import json, re, sys
from pathlib import Path
proj, name, new = Path(sys.argv[1]), sys.argv[2], int(sys.argv[3])
f = proj / name
s = f.read_text()
old = int(re.search(r'"\$preview":\{"width":\d+,"height":(\d+)\}', s).group(1))
n = s.count(f'height:{old}px')
s = s.replace(f'height:{old}px', f'height:{new}px').replace(f',"height":{old}}}', f',"height":{new}}}')
f.write_text(s)
c = json.loads((proj / 'canvas.json').read_text())
b = c['boards']; me = b[name]; me['h'] = new
(proj / 'canvas.json').write_text(json.dumps(c, indent=1, ensure_ascii=False))
hits = [k for k, v in b.items() if k != name and v['page'] == me['page'] and v['x'] < me['x'] + me['w'] and v['x'] + v['w'] > me['x'] and v['y'] < me['y'] + new + 40 and v['y'] + v['h'] > me['y']]
print(f'{name}: {old} -> {new} ({n} size rules); overlaps: {hits}')
EOF

"""Prints the chain of elements enclosing the Composer box on a board, with each one's siblings: tag start styles only."""
import re, sys
from htmlfrag import element_at, TAG
s = open(sys.argv[1]).read()
i = s.index('data-n="Composer box"')
# walk all div starts, build parent chain
stack = []
for m in TAG.finditer(s):
    if m.start() >= i: break
    close, name, selfclose = m.group(1), m.group(2), m.group(3)
    if name in ('path', 'circle', 'rect', 'line', 'polyline', 'polygon', 'img') or selfclose: continue
    if close: stack.pop()
    else: stack.append(m.start())
for a in stack[-5:]:
    tag = s[a:s.index('>', a) + 1]
    print('ANCESTOR', re.sub(r'box-sizing:border-box;flex:none;', '', tag)[:330])
    # children of this ancestor
    j = s.index('>', a) + 1; _, end = element_at(s, a)
    while j < end - 6 and s.startswith('<', j) and not s.startswith('</', j):
        c0, c1 = element_at(s, j)
        ctag = s[c0:s.index('>', c0) + 1]
        print('    child', re.sub(r'box-sizing:border-box;flex:none;', '', ctag)[:200])
        j = c1
EOF

"""Makes room for the taller Composer: the content area just above the Composer frame shrinks and clips instead of
running under the box or pushing it out of the pane. Usage: fit_content.py <canvas project dir> <board>..."""
import re, sys
from pathlib import Path
from htmlfrag import element_at, TAG
proj = Path(sys.argv[1])
for name in sys.argv[2:]:
    f = proj / name; s = f.read_text()
    i = s.index('data-n="Composer box"')
    stack = []
    for m in TAG.finditer(s):
        if m.start() >= i: break
        close, tag, selfclose = m.group(1), m.group(2), m.group(3)
        if tag in ('path', 'circle', 'rect', 'line', 'polyline', 'polygon', 'img') or selfclose: continue
        if close: stack.pop()
        else: stack.append(m.start())
    frame, pane = stack[-1], stack[-2]
    # the frame's previous sibling inside the pane
    j = s.index('>', pane) + 1; prev = None
    while j < frame:
        a, b = element_at(s, j); prev = a; j = b
    end = s.index('>', prev)
    tag = s[prev:end]
    m = re.search(r'style="([^"]*)"', tag); st = m.group(1)
    add = ''
    if 'flex:1 1 0' not in st: add += 'flex:1 1 0;'
    if 'min-height:0' not in st: add += 'min-height:0;'
    if 'overflow:hidden' not in st: st2 = st + ';overflow:hidden'
    else: st2 = st
    st2 = st2.replace('box-sizing:border-box;flex:none;', 'box-sizing:border-box;flex:none;' + add, 1) if add else st2
    s = s[:prev] + tag.replace(m.group(0), f'style="{st2}"', 1) + s[end:]
    f.write_text(s); print(name, 'added', add or '-', 'overflow')
EOF
python3 - <<'EOF'
import json
d=json.loads(open('/dev/stdin').read()) if False else None
EOF
echo ok
